page_title: Amazon Web Services In Plain English

summary.title: Amazon Web Services In Plain English
summary.one_liner: A plain-English guide to what each AWS service does, with "should have been called" renamings and comparable non-AWS products.
takeaways: Each AWS service is mapped to a plain-English purpose, such as EC2 being virtual servers and S3 being storage for assets and backups.
Many entries name a comparable non-AWS product (e.g., Heroku Postgres for RDS, RabbitMQ or Sidekiq for SQS, Redis To Go for ElastiCache).
Services are grouped into web developer, mobile developer, code deployment, enterprise, big data, and management categories.
Some services are explained as building on others, e.g., Glacier as slower archival storage for S3 and Storage Gateway as S3 connected to a corporate network.
summary.summary: This is a humorous glossary that explains over 50 AWS services in plain language. Each entry gives a "should have been called" name, a "use this to" description of the service's purpose, and often a comparison to a similar non-AWS product. The services are grouped by use case: running apps, web developer services, mobile developer services, code deployment, enterprise services, big data, and management. The page is opinionated and light on technical detail, so it works best as a quick orientation rather than a reference for configuration.
